surface supplied there.  Choose an integral ample $h\in P$ and a small
marked $P$-polarized period patch $\Omega$ about that surface, shrinking
so that $h$ stays ample.  This is an actual open image in the period
domain of $V_P$, and includes its Picard-jump fibers.

The line $z=\iota(H^{2,0}(S))$ is a point of this period domain.
Lemma~\ref{specialization:rational-density} gives $g\in O(V_P)(\Q)$
with $gz\in\Omega$.  Choose the fiber $R$ with period exactly $gz$.
Then $g\iota:T_S\to H^2(R,\Q)$ is an isometry taking the holomorphic
line to that of $R$.  The two full second-cohomology spaces have the
rational K3 form.  Witt's extension theorem extends this map to a
full rational isometry $\Phi$.  It preserves the holomorphic line,
its conjugate by rationality, and their orthogonal complement, which
is the $(1,1)$ space.  Hence $\Phi$ is Hodge.  Lefschetz $(1,1)$ gives
$\Phi(\NS(S)_{\Q})=\NS(R)_{\Q}$ and therefore $\Phi(T_S)=T_R$.
Buskin's theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Buskin} algebraizes $\Phi$ and its
inverse.  It requires neither integrality nor preservation of an ample
class.  Density was used only to enter the patch; the comparison uses
the exact realized period.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}\label{transfer:tensor}
Under the isometric-embedding hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{main:theorem},
the exact tensor $\iota_{w,E}$ on $T_S$ is algebraic for every stipulated
$w$, $E$, and transported isogenous even-Clifford model.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Choose $R,\Phi$ by Lemma~\ref{transfer:period} and set
$\phi=\Phi|_{T_S}:T_S\simeq T_R$.  The isometry induces a unital
Clifford algebra isomorphism
\[
 c_\phi:C^+(T_S,q)\xrightarrow{\sim}C^+(T_R,q),
 \qquad c_\phi(vaw)=\phi(v)c_\phi(a)\phi(w).
\]
It is a weight-one Hodge isomorphism because it takes the oriented
period bivector defining left multiplication to the corresponding
bivector for $R$.  For the broader functoriality under Hodge similarities,
see \cite[Proposition~3.1 and Lemma~3.5]{VarescoSimilarities}; the
multiplier here is one, with the prescribed right factor transported
as in the displayed identity.
Proposition~\ref{transfer:ample} gives the standard
tensor on $T_R$ for $\phi(w)$ and the polarization transported from $E$.
Precompose its cycle with the algebraic correspondence for $\Phi$ and
transport both abelian slots by $c_\phi^{-1}$.  These rational Hodge
maps on $H^1$ are algebraic by Lemma~\ref{transfer:compression}.
The displayed Clifford identity proves equality with the specified
tensor, not merely with an abstract Hodge embedding.  Source and
degree-one target projectors isolate its full action.  All operations
are degree-preserving on their intermediate factors, so the resulting
cycle has codimension two.  The same algebraic transport treats the
stipulated isogenous model.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{main:theorem}]
Proposition~\ref{transfer:tensor} proves the exact standard-tensor
assertion under the stated rational isometric-embedding hypothesis,
with every prescribed right vector, polarization, and transported model.
Choose any one such tensor and apply Theorem~\ref{ext:criterion}.
This gives rational HC and GHC in every degree of every self-power.
For an ample $P$-polarized surface, the actual transcendental space
is a nondegenerate subspace of its fixed perpendicular $U_P\simeq V_P$
by Lemma~\ref{main:lattice}, so this case is included as asserted.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Hilbert schemes and moduli spaces}

\begin{corollary}\label{transfer:moduli}
Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface admitting a rational
isometric embedding $(T_S,q)\hookrightarrow V_P$.
For every $n,r\ge1$, rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree
of $(S^{[n]})^r$, where $S^{[n]}$ is the Hilbert scheme of length-$n$
subschemes of $S$.

More generally, let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Br}(S)$ and let $M$ be either
a smooth projective moduli space of Gieseker-stable $\alpha$-twisted
sheaves on $S$, or a smooth projective moduli space of $\sigma$-stable
objects in $D^b(S,\alpha)$ for a generic Bridgeland stability condition
$\sigma$.
Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of $M^r$ for
every $r\ge1$.  If $M$ is hyperk\"ahler, the same conclusions hold for
every smooth projective hyperk\"ahler variety birational to $M$ and all
its self-powers.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The assertion for zero-dimensional $M$ is immediate.
Write $h(-)$ for the Chow motive with rational coefficients.
The decomposition of de Cataldo--Migliorini
\cite[Theorem~6.2.1]{deCataldoMigliorini} expresses $h(S^{[n]})$ as
a sum of Tate twists of summands of motives of powers of $S$; the
summands corresponding to symmetric products are cut out by rational
averaging projectors.  For either stated moduli space, B\"ulles
\cite[Theorem~0.1]{BullesModuli} likewise makes $h(M)$ a direct summand
of a finite sum of Tate twists of motives $h(S^k)$.
Tensoring these split correspondences gives analogous splittings for
every self-power, again through Tate twists of powers of $S$.
Thus these varieties are motivated by $S$ in the sense of Arapura.
Theorem~\ref{main:theorem} supplies HC and GHC for every power of $S$,
so Arapura's transfer lemma \cite[Lemma~4.2]{ArapuraMotivation},
which retains geometric coniveau with its Tate shifts, gives both
conjectures for every power of each indicated variety.
Finally, Rie\ss's specialization
correspondence for birational smooth projective hyperk\"ahler varieties
\cite[Theorem~3.2 and Section~3.3]{RiessBirational} gives an isomorphism
of Chow motives, as formulated in
\cite[Proposition~1.4]{BullesModuli}.  This proves the last assertion.
\end{proof}

statements.label: ext:criterion
statements.text: Let $S$ be a projective K3 surface. Suppose that, for one rational nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, one rational polarization, and one full even-Clifford realization, the tensor of $j_w(v)(a)=vaw$ is induced by a cycle in $\CH^2(S\times A^2)_{\Q}$. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of every self-power of $S$.

statements.label: main:theorem
statements.text: Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface. Suppose that there is a rational isometric embedding \[ (T_S,q)\hookrightarrow V_P. \] For any full even-Clifford realization $H^1(A,\Q)=C^+(T_S,q)$, any rational nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, and any rational polarization $E$ of this weight-one Hodge structure, there is a cycle \[ \Gamma_S\in\CH^2(S\times A\times A)_{\Q} \] whose action on every $x\in T_S$ is exactly $\iota_{w,E}(x)$ in $H^2(A\times A,\Q)$. The same assertion holds on a transported isogenous model with its specified tensor. Moreover, the rational Hodge conjecture and the rational generalized Hodge conjecture hold in every cohomological degree of every self-power $S^m$, for every integer $m\ge1$.

statements.label: ext:conditional
statements.text: Let $S$ be a projective K3 surface with transcendental space $(T,q)$ of rational dimension $t$, put $V=T(1)$, and let $W=C^+(T,q)=H^1(A,\Q)$ be an even-Clifford Kuga--Satake realization. Suppose that for one rational nonisotropic $w\in T$ the tensor form of \begin{equation} j_w:V\longrightarrow\End(W),\qquad j_w(v)(a)=vaw, \end{equation} is induced by a cycle in $\CH^2(S\times A^2)_{\Q}$, using a rational polarization of $W$. Then, for every $1\leq k\leq t$, there is an injective algebraic Hodge map \[ F_k:\bigwedge^kV\longrightarrow\End(W) \] with an algebraic left inverse on cohomology. More precisely, put $Z=A^2$ and $n=\dim Z$. There are correspondences \[ \Gamma_k\in\CH^{k+1}(S^k\times Z)_\Q,\qquad R_k\in\CH^{n+k-1}(Z\times S^k)_\Q. \] Viewing $\bigwedge^kV$ in $H^{2k}(S^k,\Q)(k)$ and identifying $\End(W)\simeq(H^1(A,\Q)\otimes H^1(A,\Q))(1)\subset H^2(Z,\Q)(1)$ by a rational polarization, their weight-zero actions satisfy $(\Gamma_k)_*|_{\wedge^kV}=F_k$ and $(R_k)_*F_k=\id$. Every rational Hodge class in $\bigwedge^kV$ is the class of a rational algebraic cycle of codimension $k$ on $S^k$.

statements.name: Exterior-power coniveau
statements.label: ghc:prop:exterior-coniveau
statements.text: Let $S$ satisfy the exact even-Clifford algebraicity hypothesis of Proposition \ref{ext:conditional}, and put $t=\dim_\Q T$. For every $1\le k\le t$, \[ \bigwedge^kT\subset N^{k-1}H^{2k}(S^k,\Q). \] Moreover every rational sub-Hodge structure of this exterior power satisfies the generalized Hodge conjecture in its ambient $H^{2k}(S^k,\Q)$. In particular, the top exterior line is supported in codimension $t$.

statements.label: geom:structure
statements.text: There is a smooth double cover $Y\to K=\Km(B')$, with $K$ the resolved Kummer surface, satisfying the following assertions. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The anti-invariant lattice \[ V=H^2(Y,\Z)^{\delta=-1} \] (with torsion removed) is even, has signature $(2,14)$, and has $2$-elementary discriminant group. For fixed $(B,M,\chi)$, monodromy acts trivially on this discriminant group. \item There are eight mutually orthogonal algebraic anti-invariant classes $a_1,\ldots,a_8$, each of square $-4$. Their perpendicular \[ U=\langle a_1,\ldots,a_8\rangle^\perp\subset V_\Q \] is a Hodge structure of signature $(2,6)$ and, with the intersection form inherited from $Y$, is rationally isometric to \[ V_P=(\mathbb U\oplus\mathbb U(2)\oplus D_4(-1))_\Q. \] \item Resolved pullback gives a flat Hodge isomorphism $\beta:U\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X$ with \[ (\beta x,\beta y)_X=2(x,y)_Y. \] The algebraic projector \begin{equation} e=\frac14(\Delta_X+\Gamma_j-\Gamma_\delta-\Gamma_{j\delta}) \in\CH^2(X\times X)_\Q \end{equation} has image $U_X$ in degree two and is zero in every other degree. \end{enumerate} The constructions are compatible with variation on the indicated smooth parameter opens.

statements.label: geom:period
statements.text: The period map of $U$, equivalently of $U_X$, has rank six on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the six-dimensional parameter space. For a very general parameter, its rational Hodge structure is simple, has no nonzero rational $(1,1)$-class, and has Hodge group $\SO(U)$.

statements.label: geom:domination
statements.text: For every parameter in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the parameter space, there exist smooth projective connected curves $C_1,C_2$ and a dominant generically finite morphism \[ g:C_1\times C_2\longrightarrow X. \] Whenever additionally $U_X$ has no nonzero rational $(1,1)$-class, an algebraic correspondence induces an injection \[ U_X\hookrightarrow H^1(C_1,\Q)\otimes H^1(C_2,\Q). \] In particular, this injection exists at a very general parameter.

statements.name: K3 realization of a section pencil
statements.label: pencil:realization
statements.text: Choose the abelian data and the pencil \(d_t=d_0+t d_1\) in the generic sets of Lemma \ref{geom:genericity}. There is a nonempty algebraic open \(O\subset\AA^1_t\) and a smooth projective family of K3 surfaces \(S^0\to O\) with a flat isometric embedding of rational Hodge variations \[ U\ \hookrightarrow\ R^2(S^0/O)_*\Q. \] The form on \(U\) here is its cup-product form inherited from \(Y\). For very general \(t\), this summand is the transcendental part of \(H^2(S^0_t,\Q)\). For every \(s\) in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of \(\AA^1_s\), every smooth projective model of the total family obtained by \(t=s+u^2\) is uniruled. The K3 family over \(O\) is defined over the original \(t\)-line; an additional unspecified finite base change is not part of the conclusion.

statements.name: A canonical-degree criterion
statements.label: pencil:uniruledcriterion
statements.text: Under the Weyl condition of Lemma \ref{pencil:descent}, suppose \(\deg(K_C\otimes\lambda)<0\). Every smooth projective model of the function field of \(\mathcal Z\) is uniruled.

statements.name: Two-substitution comparison
statements.label: comp:twosquares
statements.text: Let $O\subset\AA^1_t$ be a nonempty Zariski open set, and let \[ f:\mathcal S\longrightarrow O, \qquad g:\mathcal X\longrightarrow O \] be smooth projective families of connected surfaces, with the fibers of $f$ K3 surfaces. Suppose that the following conditions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item A polarized rational subvariation $\mathscr U\subset R^2f_*\Q$ of K3 type, with nondegenerate restricted cup product, is given. Its period map is nonconstant, and $U_t=\mathscr U_t$ is simple for all but countably many $t\in O$. \item There are commuting involutions $j,\delta$ of $\mathcal X$ over $O$ such that \[ e=\tfrac14(1+j)(1-\delta) \] annihilates $R^qg_*\Q$ for $q\ne2$, together with an isomorphism of rational variations of Hodge structure \[ \varphi:\mathscr U\xrightarrow{\sim}eR^2g_*\Q. \] \item For $s$ in a nonempty Zariski open subset of $\AA^1$, the total spaces of the two surface families pulled back by $t=s+u^2$ have smooth projective uniruled threefold models. \end{enumerate} Then there are a nonempty Zariski open set $G\subset O$ and a countable set $E\subset G$ such that, for every $b\in G\setminus E$, a correspondence \[ \Theta_b\in\CH^2(S_b\times X_b)_\Q \] induces $\varphi_b$ on $U_b$. The open set $G$ and all auxiliary correspondences used before the choice of $b$ can be fixed for the given pencil.

statements.label: comp:surface
statements.text: Fix abelian-cover data and a section pencil for which \Cref{geom:structure,geom:period,pencil:realization} apply, with nonconstant $U$-period along the pencil and simple $U_t$ outside a countable set. On a nonempty open of that pencil, for all but countably many $b$, there is an algebraic correspondence \[ \Theta_b\in\CH^2(S_b^0\times X_b)_\Q \] whose action on $U_b$ is the given identification with $H^2(X_b)^{j=+,\,\delta=-}$.

statements.label: final:generic
statements.text: Let $b$ be a construction point of Lemma \ref{final:curves}, and let $S$ be a projective K3 surface equipped with a rational Hodge isometry $r_T:T_S\xrightarrow{\sim}U_b=T_{S_b^0}$ for the cup-product forms. For every full even-Clifford model $A$ of $T_S$, every rational nonisotropic right factor $w$, and every rational polarization $E$, there is a cycle \[ \Gamma_S\in\CH^2(S\times A\times A)_\Q, \qquad (\Gamma_S)_*x=\iota_{w,E}(x)\quad(x\in T_S), \] where the equality holds in $H^2(A\times A,\Q)$.

statements.label: specialization:ambient
statements.text: Let $S$ have an ample primitive $P$-polarization and put $U_P=P_{\Q}^{\perp}\subset H^2(S,\Q)$. There are a full even-Clifford realization $W_U=C^+(U_P,q)=H^1(A_U,\Q)$, a rational polarization $E_0$, a nonisotropic rational $w_0\in U_P$, and a cycle \[ \Gamma_U\in\CH^2(S\times A_U^2)_{\Q} \] whose full degree-two action on every $x\in U_P$ is exactly $\iota_{w_0,E_0}(x)$. This assertion concerns the whole fixed rank-eight space, including its rational $(1,1)$ classes at a Picard jump.

statements.label: transfer:ample
statements.text: Let $S$ be an ample $P$-polarized K3 surface. For every prescribed nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, rational polarization $E$ and transported even-Clifford realization of $C^+(T_S,q)$, its standard tensor $\iota_{w,E}$ has a rational codimension-two algebraic realization.

statements.label: transfer:tensor
statements.text: Under the isometric-embedding hypothesis of Theorem \ref{main:theorem}, the exact tensor $\iota_{w,E}$ on $T_S$ is algebraic for every stipulated $w$, $E$, and transported isogenous even-Clifford model.

statements.label: transfer:moduli
statements.text: Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface admitting a rational isometric embedding $(T_S,q)\hookrightarrow V_P$. For every $n,r\ge1$, rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of $(S^{[n]})^r$, where $S^{[n]}$ is the Hilbert scheme of length-$n$ subschemes of $S$. More generally, let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Br}(S)$ and let $M$ be either a smooth projective moduli space of Gieseker-stable $\alpha$-twisted sheaves on $S$, or a smooth projective moduli space of $\sigma$-stable objects in $D^b(S,\alpha)$ for a generic Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma$. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of $M^r$ for every $r\ge1$. If $M$ is hyperk\"ahler, the same conclusions hold for every smooth projective hyperk\"ahler variety birational to $M$ and all its self-powers.
